title: Finite Joint Adjustment Sets in Summary Causal Graphs with a Known Maximum Lag
banked_reason: D0.5.G: delivered tier=subfield below field floor; paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4, with both math and decision panels PASS and no unrepaired findings.
gap_reasons: It does not establish probabilistic identification or completeness for arbitrary bi-infinite SCM laws, so the setup's interventional-distribution target is supported only conditional on external operational semantics, regular conditionals, and positivity.

The stationary-cost result proves existence of a finite optimizer family through a nonconstructive count-vector argument but supplies neither the family nor an effective temporal radius, leaving the advertised optimization consequence unusable algorithmically.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the exact outgoing-tail boundary replacement and finite-core reduction for the time-varying bounded-lag anchor class, finite orientation saturation, and a fixed-graph ladder separating finite feasibility from uniformly bounded minimal or time-dependent-cost-optimal histories. Both mathematical panels passed, but the field-tier package failed because extending the result to probabilistic completeness for bi-infinite SCMs or making the stationary-cost radius effective would require a materially new research program; those are the natural re-raise directions.
tldr: Does a known maximum lag make universal joint generalized-adjustment feasibility exactly finite even though inclusion-minimal histories and optima under positive time-dependent acquisition costs can occur arbitrarily far in the past? We prove that every universally valid history can be replaced by the outgoing-tail portion of the \(L\)-slice pre-intervention boundary plus a finite core. For the possibly time-varying bounded-lag anchor class, finite-core uncertainty reduces to one strict-lag saturated core or at most \((n!)^{b-a+1}\) per-slice-order cores; under a stationary edge template, the sharper bounds are one strict-lag template or at most \(n!\) globally ordered instantaneous templates. A fixed three-series lag-one singleton class has inclusion-minimal histories and unique optima for suitable positive time-dependent costs at unbounded ages. For each of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{tv}}(S,L)\) and \(\mathcal C(S,L)\) separately, stationary per-series costs admit an existential finite optimizer family with \(\min_Z|Z|\leq L|O_S|+n(b-a+1)-|X|-1\). No effective value of \(\rho_{\mathrm{tv}}\) or \(\rho_{\mathrm{stat}}\) is supplied, both questions remain open, and no transfer between them is proved.
gap: Current SCG theory decides common adjustment and constructs canonical histories, and narrower bounded-lag work constructs finite sets, but the inspected sources do not show that every arbitrary valid joint-adjustment history has an exact radius-​\(L\) replacement. Nor do they characterize whether finite feasibility controls all minimal or cost-optimal histories.
fill: Prove edge-saturation and boundary-replacement theorems with explicit finite bounds, then prove a fixed-graph ladder obstruction with path-by-path indispensability and cost certificates; retain stationary-cost compactness as a sharply delimited positive result and an effective-radius question as future work.
